ev-arab-conquest-of-egypt:coord.reason: Wikidata's point (28, 32.1) is a generic centroid of Egypt. Our marker at Babylon/Fustat (Old Cairo) is the site of the decisive siege of 640–641 and of the garrison town founded afterwards (Kennedy; Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam).
checked: Hugh Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007), ch. 4

ev-muslim-conquest-of-the-maghreb:coord.reason: Wikidata's (30, 5) is a point in the Algerian Sahara. Our marker is Kairouan, the base founded by ʿUqba ibn Nafiʿ in 670, and the full campaign path is given as a route.
checked: UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III, ch. 9

ev-founding-of-marrakesh:year.reason: The chronicles disagree: Ibn Abi Zarʿ and Ibn Khaldun give 1062, Ibn ʿIdhari gives 1070. Bennison and most recent scholarship follow 1070, and Britannica says only 'mid-11th century'. Wikidata's 1065 matches neither. We keep 1070 at medium confidence, and the note now states the dispute.
checked: Britannica: Marrakech (search snippet: 'founded in the mid-11th century')
Amira K. Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

ev-battle-of-ridaniya:coord.reason: The battle was fought at al-Raydaniyya, just north-east of Cairo (modern ʿAbbasiyya). Wikidata's (27, 29) is a point in the Western Desert.
checked: Ibn Iyas, Badaʾiʿ al-Zuhur, as cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ridaniya

ev-ethiopian-adal-war:coord.reason: Wikidata's (9, 40) is a generic Horn of Africa point. Our marker is near Wayna Daga, east of Lake Tana, where the decisive battle of 1543 was fought; the note says the war ranged over the whole highlands.
checked: Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)

ev-fula-jihads-sokoto:year.reason: 1804 is correct for Usman dan Fodio's jihad (Britannica: 1804–08). The diff came from a wrong-scope QID: Q2736105 covers the whole series of Fula jihads from 1725. The record now uses Q16707899 (Jihad of Usman dan Fodio, 21 February 1804–1808).

ev-fula-jihads-sokoto:coord.reason: Wikidata's (12, 3) is a point near the Niger–Benin border, not a jihad site. Our marker is Sokoto, the caliphate's capital; the stops for Usman dan Fodio give Degel, Gudu and Alkalawa.

ev-french-conquest-of-algeria:coord.reason: Wikidata's (28, 1) is a Saharan centroid. Our marker is Algiers, taken on 5 July 1830 after the landing at Sidi Ferruch on 14 June.

ev-scramble-for-africa:year.reason: 1881, the French protectorate over Tunisia, is the start most historians use. Pakenham begins in 1876 and Wikidata starts with the Berlin Act of 1885. The record is already medium confidence with a note on the convention.
checked: Thomas Pakenham, The Scramble for Africa 1876–1912 (1991)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VII (1985), ch. 2

ev-second-boer-war:coord.reason: Wikidata's (-29, 24) is a centroid of South Africa. Our marker is Pretoria, capital of the South African Republic, which was taken in June 1900; the Treaty of Vereeniging was signed there in 1902.

ev-herero-and-nama-genocide:coord.reason: Wikidata's (-22, 17) is a centroid of Namibia. Our marker is the Waterberg, site of the battle of 11 August 1904, after which von Trotha drove the Herero into the Omaheke.

ev-maji-maji-war:coord.reason: Wikidata's coordinate (-2.41, 30.54) lies in Rwanda, outside the war zone. The rising began in the Matumbi Hills inland from Kilwa in July 1905, and our marker is there.
checked: John Iliffe, A Modern History of Tanganyika (1979), ch. 6

ev-second-italo-ethiopian-war:coord.reason: Addis Ababa, occupied on 5 May 1936, is the natural marker for the capital's fall. Wikidata's point near Gondar is not a defining site of the war. The end year of 1936 also stands: Bahru Zewde dates the conventional war 1935–36.
checked: Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia (2001)

ev-mau-mau-uprising:coord.reason: Wikidata's point (-4.04, 39.67) is Mombasa, on the coast, outside the conflict zone. The insurgency centred on the central highlands (Nyeri, Aberdares, Mount Kenya), and our marker is at Nyeri.
checked: David Anderson, Histories of the Hanged (2005)

ev-african-union-launched:year.reason: Britannica says the AU officially came into being on 9 July 2002 at the Durban summit. 1999, Wikidata's value, is the Sirte Declaration that proposed it, and the Constitutive Act entered into force in May 2001.

ev-african-union-launched:coord.reason: The event is the launch summit, so it is marked at Durban. Wikidata's (0, 15) is a continental centroid for the organisation, not a site.

ev-tunisian-revolution:coord.reason: The revolution began with Bouazizi's self-immolation in Sidi Bouzid; Wikidata's (34, 10) is a national centroid. Separately, the start date was corrected from 18 to 17 December 2010.

polity-ayyubid-egypt:to.reason: 1250 was the correct end of the Ayyubid sultanate in Egypt; Wikidata's 1341 counts the Syrian branches (Hama). The record has since been removed from data/africa as a duplicate of west-asia's polity-ayyubid (same QID Q180114).
checked: R. Stephen Humphreys, From Saladin to the Mongols (1977)

polity-ghana-empire:from.reason: Britannica cites an unconfirmed tradition dating the kingdom's origins to the 4th century CE, which our 300 reflects. Wikidata's c. 100 has weaker support. The record stays low confidence, and its note says the origins are unknown.
checked: Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

polity-zagwe:from.reason: Britannica places the Zagwe in the 12th–13th centuries, and c. 1137 is the conventional start date. The c. 900 start in Wikidata rests on late Solomonic traditions that give the dynasty a much longer span. The record remains low confidence and its note records the dispute.
checked: Taddesse Tamrat, Church and State in Ethiopia 1270–1527 (1972)

polity-marinid:from.reason: Britannica says the Banu Marin advanced into Morocco in the 1240s, took Fez in 1248 and Marrakesh in 1269. 1244 is the accession of Abu Yahya and the usual start of the dynasty proper; Wikidata's 1215 marks the first tribal incursions.

polity-benin-kingdom:from.reason: All the start dates are traditional. 1180 (Eweka I, Egharevba's chronology) and Wikidata's 1170 differ by a decade, Britannica puts Eweka in the 13th century, and the Ogiso kingdom goes back to c. 900. Kept at 1180, medium confidence, with an explicit note.

polity-kongo:to.reason: Curator moved the end from 1888 to 1914 (REPORT-africa note). Portugal abolished the titular Kongo monarchy in 1914 after suppressing the 1913–14 revolt; Wikidata's 1888 is the date of formal vassalage, when the kingdom still existed. Record is medium with a note.

ev-vandalic-war:coord.reason: Wikidata’s (30.44, 9.68) is a point in the Sahara. The war was decided around Carthage (Ad Decimum, Tricamarum), and the record carries the full campaign route from Caput Vada to Mount Papua.

ev-great-mosque-of-kairouan-rebuilt:year.reason: Wikidata dates the building’s first foundation by ʿUqba ibn Nafiʿ (670). This record marks the reconstruction by Ziyadat Allah I in 836, which gave the mosque its present form; the 670 foundation is covered by ev-muslim-conquest-of-the-maghreb.
checked: Jonathan M. Bloom, Architecture of the Islamic West (2020)

ev-ife-heads:year.reason: Wikidata’s 1100 is the start of the Ife classical period. Most of the copper-alloy heads are dated to the 14th–early 15th century (British Museum; Drewal and Schildkrout 2009), so the marker year is 1300 with medium confidence and a note.

ev-ife-heads:coord.reason: Wikidata’s (9, 8) is a centroid of Nigeria. The heads were found in Ile-Ife (Wunmonije compound, 1938), where our marker is.

ev-rosetta-stone-found:year.reason: The QID is the object, which Wikidata dates by its creation (196 BCE). This event is the discovery near Rashid in July 1799.

ev-rosetta-stone-found:coord.reason: Wikidata’s coordinate is the British Museum in London, the object’s present location. The event marker is the find-spot at Fort Julien near Rashid (Rosetta).

ev-british-expedition-to-abyssinia:coord.reason: Wikidata places the expedition at Gondar, which Napier never reached. The decisive actions were at Arogee and Magdala (Amba Mariam), where our marker is; the route gives the march from Zula.
checked: Richard Pankhurst, The Napier Expedition and the Loot from Maqdala (1985)

ev-angolan-civil-war:coord.reason: Wikidata’s (-12.35, 17.35) is a centroid of Angola. Our marker is Luanda, where independence was proclaimed under fire on 11 November 1975 and which the MPLA held throughout.

ev-truth-and-reconciliation-commission:e.reason: 1998 is the year the commission’s hearings ended and its five-volume report was presented to President Mandela (29 October 1998). The amnesty committee worked on until 2001 and the final volumes were published in 2003; Wikidata’s 2002 is one of these later milestones.

ev-south-sudan-independence:coord.reason: The QID is the country, so Wikidata gives a national centroid. Independence was proclaimed in Juba on 9 July 2011, where our marker is.

ev-west-african-ebola-epidemic:coord.reason: Wikidata’s (12, 3) is a generic West Africa point in Niger, far from the outbreak. Our marker is Meliandou, Guinea, where WHO investigators traced the index case of December 2013.

person-dihya:born.reason: No source gives a birth year; Wikidata’s 668 and our 640 are both estimates (she is said to have been old at her death c. 703). The record is low confidence with a note.

person-idris-alooma:born.reason: Wikidata’s 1580 cannot be right: Idris Alooma began to reign in 1564 (Lange) or c. 1571 (older chronology). Our 1540 is a placeholder; the record is low confidence with a note.

person-sunni-ali:born.reason: Wikidata’s 1464 is the year Sunni Ali became king, not his birth. His birth year is unknown; ours is a placeholder, stated in the note.

person-yaa-asantewaa:born.reason: Sources give c. 1832, c. 1840 and c. 1850. We follow c. 1840 (Boahen; most reference works). The record is medium confidence with a note.
checked: A. Adu Boahen, Yaa Asantewaa and the Asante–British War of 1900–1 (2003)

polity-kush:from.reason: Wikidata dates Kush from Kerma times. The record deliberately covers the Meroitic period, when the capital was at Meroë (from c. 300 BCE); its name and note say so.
checked: László Török, The Kingdom of Kush (1997)

polity-darfur-sultanate:from.reason: Wikidata gives 1603 (the Keira origin tradition); O’Fahey dates the historical sultanate to Sulayman Solongdungu in the 1640s–60s. We keep 1640 at medium confidence with a note.
checked: R. S. O’Fahey, The Darfur Sultanate (2008)

polity-darfur-sultanate:to.reason: Wikidata ends the sultanate at its conquest by al-Zubayr in 1874. Ali Dinar restored it in 1898 and it lasted until the British conquest of 1916; the note records the 1874–1898 interruption.
checked: R. S. O’Fahey, The Darfur Sultanate (2008)

polity-kano:to.reason: Wikidata’s 1349 is the conversion of the Kano court to Islam under Yaji I. The Hausa kingdom lasted until the Fulani jihad deposed Muhammad Alwali II in 1807.
checked: The Kano Chronicle, trans. H. R. Palmer (1928)

polity-ndongo:from.reason: Both dates are conventional: c. 1515 is the usual date for Ngola Kiluanje kia Samba’s break from Kongo overlordship, and 1518 is the year of Ndongo’s first embassy to Portugal. We keep 1515 at medium confidence.
checked: Linda M. Heywood, Njinga of Angola (2017)

polity-ndongo:to.reason: Ndongo ended when the Portuguese took Pungo Andongo and the last king, João Hari II, in November 1671 (Lara 2016; EBSCO). Wikidata’s 1683 appears to refer to later wars with Matamba.

polity-buganda:from.reason: Both dates are traditional (14th–15th century). Kiwanuka’s king lists place the founder Kintu c. 1400; the record is low confidence with a note.
checked: M. S. M. Semakula Kiwanuka, A History of Buganda (1972)

ev-franco-hova-war-1895:endYear.reason: Reviewer switched the QID from the combined Franco-Hova Wars item to the second Madagascar expedition (1894–95), which Wikidata ends in 1895 with the fall of Antananarivo. This record deliberately runs on through the menalamba rising, the annexation of 1896 and Gallieni’s abolition of the monarchy in February 1897 (Britannica: Madagascar, history; Brown, A History of Madagascar).

polity-lunda:to.reason: Wikidata’s 1884 is the start of the colonial partition. The Lunda state kept its Musumba and Mwaant Yav until Chokwe invaders took the capital in 1887 (Wikipedia infobox; Vansina, Kingdoms of the Savanna); partition between Angola, the Congo Free State and Rhodesia ran 1884–1891. Record is low confidence with a note.

ev-franco-hova-war-1895:coord.reason: Wikidata’s (-20, 47) is a centroid of Madagascar. Our marker is Antananarivo, whose surrender on 30 September 1895 ended the campaign; the route gives the march from Mahajanga.
checked: Stephen Ellis, The Rising of the Red Shawls (1985)
